Thanks for the ping, Avery. Reviewed MedGen's proposed language and flagged the items below. I've attached a counter-redline (redline_avery_v2.pdf) with inline comments. High level: we cannot accept unrestricted runtime exports or long retention of raw request/response pairs. Two acceptable paths from a legal/compliance perspective: 

Option A — Narrow export scope (preferred):
- Allow exports only for discrete, customer-requested job-ids tied to support tickets or escalations
- Exports must be pre-approved by Redwood Security & Product, delivered as a sanitized package (PII redaction + hashed identifiers), and limited to 30 days retention on Redwood systems
- Customer may store delivered export for their purposes, but Redwood disclaims liability for customer-handled copies

Option B — Enclave export (if MedGen insists on raw data):
- Export via encrypted enclave that MedGen can access only with their KMS keys (customer-managed KMS); we require indemnity & SOC2 evidence for enclave usage
- Retention strictly limited to 14 days in the enclave

Blockers / absolute no-go items:
- Any clause allowing MedGen to demand an on-demand dump of the production KV cache or model training data (explicitly forbidden)
- Unlimited retention of raw request/response pairs on Redwood systems

Priya — please run a quick security checklist: transport mechanism (SFTP vs. HTTPS with pre-signed link), encryption at rest, access logging, and whether KMS integration for enclave flow is on roadmap. Marcus — need a product estimate (hours, infra changes) for Option A vs Option B and an assessment of UX/ops overhead. This will let us pick a tradeoff to present to MedGen.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Short answer: Option A looks viable and lowest risk. Quick notes from product assessment: 

- Feasibility: We can add an export job that assembles request/response pairs for specific job-ids and runs sanitization (PII patterns + drop embeddings). No model changes required; mostly infra and export tooling (~3-4 sprint-weeks for an initial MVP + 1-2 weeks ops hardening).
- Retention: 30-day window is reasonable; default auto-delete pipeline should be implemented.
- Delivery: Secure pre-signed HTTPS link (time-limited) is simpler than SFTP and avoids opening firewall rules. We can encrypt the bundle with customer-provided public key if needed.
- Cost & perf: Small additional storage + occasional CPU during export; negligible impact on serving latency but requires an ops playbook and runbook.

Ask: Priya/Olga can we agree to Option A with these specifics: 30-day sanitized retention, exported within 14 days of request, delivered via time-limited pre-signed HTTPS link, and Redwood requires a signed NDA/indemnity covering customer-handled copies? If yes, I'll draft a short technical appendix (runtime_export_schema.xlsx) describing the export package and steps and can include an estimated timeline for the pilot.

Marcus Lin
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
